```{r setup}
#| include: false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(sf); library(ggplot2); library(glue)
  library(patchwork); library(knitr); library(scales); library(purrr); library(readr)
  library(stringr); library(ggrepel)
})
source("R/00_config.R"); source("R/helpers.R"); source("R/huff_core.R")
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "en_US.UTF-8"))  # R runs in the C locale here; keeps R² and × intact

# The helpers read PAL at call time, so overriding it converts every figure in
# the deck to the dark palette without touching a plot definition.
PAL <- modifyList(PAL, list(
  ink = "#F4E7DF", ground = "#2B1512", rule = "#593029", muted = "#C3A79B",
  land = "#4A2822", land_line = "#2B1512", null = "#5A3A33",
  accent = "#5FB3BC", accent_lt = "#2F6E75", loss = "#F0864B", loss_lt = "#9E4A40",
  div = c("#F0864B", "#D08A6C", "#A98C82", "#8C8580", "#7FA3A6", "#5FB3BC", "#A9DCE0")))

# Every number on these slides is read from the pipeline's outputs.
origins  <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "origins.rds"))
stations <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "stations.rds"))
cal      <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "calibration.rds"))
scn      <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "scenario.rds"))
va       <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "value_added.rds"))
r5       <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "scenario_r5.rds"))
sens     <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "sensitivity.rds"))
D        <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "diagnostics.rds"))
taps_m   <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "taps_by_month.rds"))
subzone  <- st_read(F_SUBZONE, quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(STUDY_CRS) |>
  st_make_valid() |> select(SUBZONE_N, PLN_AREA_N, REGION_N)
stn <- cal$stn; th <- cal$fits[[cal$best]]$theta; res <- scn$res; ci <- cal$cal_idx
ex <- filter(stations, existing); n_fit <- length(ci); newS <- filter(stations, new)
cmp <- sens$comparison; m_of <- function(m, col) cmp[[col]][cmp$model == m]
pct <- function(x) percent(x, accuracy = 1); num <- function(x, a = 1) comma(x, accuracy = a)
lines_sf <- function(s) s |> mutate(kind = case_when(new & str_detect(lines_2030, "JRL") ~ "Jurong Region Line",
                                                     new & str_detect(lines_2030, "CRL") ~ "Cross Island Line",
                                                     TRUE ~ "Existing"))
mapt <- function(base = 13, crop = TRUE) list(if (crop) sg_crop(stations) else coord_sf(expand = FALSE, datum = NA),
                                             theme_map(base_size = base))
kf <- function(...) {
  items <- list(...)
  cat('<div class="kf">')
  for (it in items) cat(sprintf('<div><div class="n">%s</div><div class="l">%s</div></div>', it[[1]], it[[2]]))
  cat('</div>')
}
nn <- res |> filter(new) |> arrange(-pred_2030)
q10 <- quantile(stn$tap_am[ci], 0.1)
low <- nn |> filter(pred_2030 < q10)
mon_cor <- taps_m |> select(YEAR_MONTH, pt_code, tap_am) |> pivot_wider(names_from = YEAR_MONTH, values_from = tap_am) |>
  select(-pt_code) |> log() |> cor(use = "complete.obs")
lr <- va$lambda_region |> mutate(region = str_to_title(sub(" REGION", "", region)))
lrv <- function(r) sprintf("%.1f", lr$lambda[lr$region == r])
src <- "Source: LTA DataMall Passenger Volume by Train Stations, Aug to Oct 2026; HDB (data.gov.sg); own Huff model."
```

## Contents {.smaller}

::: {.subhead}
One question: where do HDB residents board the train on weekday mornings, and how would
the planned Jurong Region Line (JRL) and Cross Island Line phase 1 (CRL) change that?
:::

1. Why station demand is needed before a station opens
2. The data, and how far they can be trusted
3. How the model shares out each block's residents
4. What makes a station attract riders
5. How accurate the model is
6. Which new stations have the most HDB residents nearby
7. Where boardings move when the new lines open
8. How catchments change in the west
9. Whether distance matters equally everywhere
10. What planners can and cannot take from this

## Planners need an estimate of station demand before anyone has used the station

```{r}
#| output: asis
kf(list(num(nrow(origins)), "HDB blocks"),
   list(paste0(round(sum(origins$du) / 1e6, 2), "M"), "dwelling units"),
   list(sum(stations$existing), "stations today"),
   list(sum(stations$new), "new JRL and CRL stations"))
```

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-map}
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-width: 7.2
s_all <- lines_sf(stations)
ggplot() + base_land(subzone) +
  geom_sf(data = origins, aes(size = du), colour = "#B79A8E", alpha = 0.35, stroke = 0) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(s_all, kind == "Existing"), shape = 21, fill = PAL$ground, colour = PAL$ink, size = 1.1, stroke = 0.4) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(s_all, kind != "Existing"), aes(fill = kind), shape = 21, colour = PAL$ground, size = 2.4, stroke = 0.4) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 1.5, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Jurong Region Line" = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]], "Cross Island Line" = LINE_COLS[["CRL"]]), name = NULL) +
  mapt(11)
```
:::
::: {.note}
Stations open late when their riders are not there: Hume waited ten years, Buangkok
and Woodleigh stayed shut when their line opened.

**The question.** Where do HDB residents board on weekday mornings (06:00 to 09:00),
and how would the JRL and CRL phase 1 change that? LTA currently schedules both by 2030.

**Why mornings, why HDB.** Morning trips mostly start at home, so boardings can be
traced to nearby homes. HDB flats house about four in five residents and are the only
homes counted block by block.

*Grey dots: HDB blocks, sized by flats. Teal and green: the new stations.*
:::
:::

## The data were usable only after four traps were cleared

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-inout}
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 6.6
d <- ex |> st_drop_geometry() |> mutate(in_fit = du_1km >= CAL_MIN_DU_1KM)
lab <- d |> filter(name %in% c("Yishun", "Woodlands", "Raffles Place", "Newton", "Kranji", "Tuas Link", "Punggol"))
ggplot(d, aes(tapout_am, tap_am)) +
  geom_abline(colour = PAL$muted, linewidth = 0.3, linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = in_fit), size = 2, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_text_repel(data = lab, aes(label = name), size = 3.4, colour = PAL$ink, seed = 1, min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma()) + scale_y_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = PAL$accent, `FALSE` = PAL$loss),
                      labels = c(`TRUE` = "HDB homes nearby: used to fit", `FALSE` = "Few HDB homes: not used"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Morning tap-outs per month", y = "Morning tap-ins per month") +
  theme_ex03(13, grid = "both")
```
:::
::: {.note}
**No shared key** between HDB's flat counts and its building outlines: one OneMap
lookup per street linked all 10,817 blocks.

**LTA's station layer holds unopened shells** (Bukit Brown, Mount Pleasant, Marina
South). The passenger data, not the layer, decides what operates.

**Circle Line stage 6 opened on 12 July 2026**, though listed as planned: moved to
today's network.

**JS2A is not one of the JRL's 24 stations**: LTA plans it for the mid-2030s.

The counts are steady (month-to-month correlation `r round(mon_cor[1, 3], 2)`).
Below the dashed line, a station receives more people than it sends out in the morning.
`r with(st_drop_geometry(ex), sum(du_1km < CAL_MIN_DU_1KM & tap_am < tapout_am))` of the
`r sum(ex$du_1km < CAL_MIN_DU_1KM)` stations with few HDB homes nearby sit there, so they are
kept as competitors but not used to fit the model.
:::
:::

## The model shares each block's residents among nearby stations by distance and pull

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-example}
#| fig-height: 3.9
#| fig-width: 6.8
eg <- "220A | TENGAH GDN WALK"
d <- bind_rows(scn$sh_now |> filter(origin_id == eg) |> mutate(network = "Today"),
               scn$sh_30 |> filter(origin_id == eg) |> mutate(network = "With JRL and CRL")) |>
  group_by(network) |> slice_max(p, n = 4) |> ungroup() |> mutate(new = name %in% newS$name)
ggplot(d, aes(p, reorder(name, p), fill = new)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.62) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pct(p)), hjust = -0.15, size = 4, colour = PAL$ink) +
  facet_wrap(~network, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = PAL$accent_lt, `TRUE` = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]]), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))) +
  labs(x = "Share of the block's residents", y = NULL) + theme_ex03(13, grid = "x")
```
:::
::: {.note}
$$
P_{ij} = \frac{A_j\, d_{ij}^{\lambda}}{\sum_{l} A_l\, d_{il}^{\lambda}}
$$

**One block in Tengah (220A Tengah Garden Walk).** Today its residents are spread over
four stations, none of them near. With the JRL, two new stations take most of them.

Each station within 3 km scores higher the closer it is (distance $d$) and the more it
offers (attractiveness $A$). Residents are shared in proportion to the scores, and each
station's boardings are the homes it draws times one trip rate.

**Fitted** to the 148 stations with HDB homes nearby; the shares match the course's
`MCI` package to 15 decimal places.
:::
:::

## Stations with more lines and more around them draw more riders; LRT-only stops far fewer

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-params}
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 6.6
lab_terms <- c(lambda = "Distance (exponent)", n_lines = "Lines served", bus_stops = "Bus stops nearby",
               poi = "Shops and services nearby", lrt_only = "LRT-only station")
p <- tibble(term = names(th), estimate = th) |> left_join(cal$ci, by = "term") |>
  mutate(term = factor(lab_terms[term], rev(lab_terms)))
ggplot(p, aes(estimate, term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = PAL$muted, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0, colour = PAL$accent, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(colour = PAL$accent, size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", estimate)), vjust = -1, size = 3.8, colour = PAL$ink) +
  labs(x = "Estimate with 95% bootstrap interval (right of zero: more attractive)", y = NULL) +
  theme_ex03(13, grid = "x")
```
:::
::: {.note}
Holding the rest fixed, the model estimates:

**A second line: ×`r round((3/2)^th[["n_lines"]], 1)`** the pull of a one-line station.

**Ten times the shops and services: ×`r round(10^th[["poi"]], 1)`.**

**LRT-only: `r pct(exp(th[["lrt_only"]]))`** of the pull of a similar MRT station.

**Twice as far: ÷`r round(2^-th[["lambda"]], 1)`.** Bus stops add nothing once the
rest is known.

[These are associations, not proven causes: saving a transfer is a plausible reason
interchanges draw more, but the model cannot show it. The distance and LRT estimates
trade off against each other (LRT stops sit close to their blocks), so only their
combined effect is firm.]{.caveat}
:::
:::

## The model ranks stations well but misses any one station by about a third

```{r}
#| output: asis
kf(list(pct(m_of("M0", "R2_log")), "textbook Huff, R² on hidden stations"),
   list(pct(m_of("M3", "R2_log")), "this model, R² on hidden stations"),
   list(sprintf("%.2f", m_of("M3", "spearman")), "rank correlation"),
   list(paste0(round(m_of("M3", "MdAPE_pct")), "%"), "typical miss, one station"))
```

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-obs}
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 6.6
d <- st_drop_geometry(stn)[ci, ] |> mutate(cv = cal$cv_pred[[cal$best]][ci], err = log(tap_am / cv))
lab <- d |> slice_max(abs(err), n = 6)
ggplot(d, aes(cv, tap_am)) +
  geom_abline(colour = PAL$muted, linewidth = 0.4, linetype = 2) +
  geom_abline(intercept = log10(2), colour = PAL$muted, linewidth = 0.25, linetype = 3) +
  geom_abline(intercept = -log10(2), colour = PAL$muted, linewidth = 0.25, linetype = 3) +
  geom_point(colour = PAL$accent, size = 1.9, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(data = lab, aes(label = name), size = 3.3, colour = PAL$ink, seed = 2, min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma()) + scale_y_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Predicted with its own ridership hidden", y = "Observed morning tap-ins per month") +
  theme_ex03(13, grid = "both")
```
:::
::: {.note}
Each station was predicted with its own ridership hidden (10-fold cross-validation),
the closest available test of predicting a new station.

**Rank:** nearly right. **One station:** typically `r round(m_of("M3", "MdAPE_pct"))`% off;
the dotted lines mark a factor of two.

**Misses cluster in space** (Moran's I `r round(D$moran_perm$statistic, 2)`, permutation
p = `r D$moran_perm$p.value`): too low beside private housing the model cannot see, too
high at recently opened Keppel.

[A high score on existing stations is not proof for new ones. No real opening could be
tested: DataMall keeps only three months of data.]{.caveat}
:::
:::

## Tengah Plantation, Serangoon North and Pasir Ris East have the most HDB residents nearby

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-new}
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-width: 6.6
d <- nn |> mutate(name = reorder(name, pred_2030), line = ifelse(line_new == "JRL", "JRL", "CRL"))
ggplot(d, aes(pred_2030, name)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = q10, xmax = quantile(stn$tap_am[ci], 0.5), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = PAL$land) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = pred_2030_lo, xmax = pred_2030_hi, colour = line), height = 0, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = line), size = 2.2) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(JRL = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]], CRL = LINE_COLS[["CRL"]]), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Modelled morning boardings per month from HDB homes (log scale)", y = NULL) +
  theme_ex03(11.5, grid = "x")
```
:::
::: {.note}
**Top:** stations placed among HDB blocks with no station today. Tengah Plantation
(`r num(nn$pred_2030[nn$name == "Tengah Plantation"], 1000)` a month), Serangoon North
(`r num(nn$pred_2030[nn$name == "Serangoon North"], 1000)`) and Pasir Ris East
(`r num(nn$pred_2030[nn$name == "Pasir Ris East"], 1000)`).

**Bottom:** `r nrow(low)` stations below today's 10th percentile, in industrial,
university and airport areas. That means few HDB homes are near them, **not** that they
will be little used: their riders are workers, students and travellers, whom this model
does not count.

*Shaded band: today's stations, 10th to 50th percentile.*

[Bars show parameter uncertainty only, not the range of real ridership. Homes and
surroundings are held at today's.]{.caveat}
:::
:::

## The new lines move boardings between stations; they do not add them

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-bars}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 6.6
d <- res |> filter(existing, !is.na(change)) |> filter(rank(change) <= 12 | change > 0) |>
  mutate(name = reorder(name, change), dir = ifelse(change > 0, "gain", "loss"))
ggplot(d, aes(change, name, fill = dir)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pct(change_pct), hjust = ifelse(change > 0, -0.15, 1.15)), size = 3.6, colour = PAL$ink) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = PAL$ink, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(gain = PAL$accent, loss = PAL$loss), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.2, 0.22))) +
  labs(x = "Change in modelled morning boardings per month", y = NULL) +
  theme_ex03(12, grid = "x")
```
:::
::: {.note}
The model keeps the number of homes and trips fixed, so total morning boardings are
exactly the same before and after. Only where people board changes.

**Largest losses:** stations that the new lines run between. Chinese Garden, Lakeside
and Pioneer lose blocks to the JRL's Jurong West branch, Kovan to Serangoon North and
Tavistock.

**Only gains:** the four stations that become Cross Island Line interchanges (Hougang,
Bright Hill, Ang Mo Kio, Pasir Ris).

[Fewer people entering a station does not mean emptier trains: many JRL riders will
still change to the East-West Line. Train loads need a routing model.]{.caveat}
:::
:::

## Tengah and Jurong West gain stations of their own

```{r sl-market}
#| fig-height: 4.7
#| fig-width: 11.5
west <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(c(xmin = 11000, xmax = 23500, ymin = 31000, ymax = 42500), crs = st_crs(STUDY_CRS)))
o_w <- origins |> st_filter(west) |> left_join(scn$dom, by = "origin_id")
top <- union(names(sort(table(o_w$station_now), decreasing = TRUE))[1:12], names(sort(table(o_w$station_2030), decreasing = TRUE))[1:14])
pal_st <- setNames(rep_len(c("#5FB3BC", "#F0864B", "#8FA8D6", "#E3B566", "#7CC38B", "#C79BD0", "#4C9AB0", "#E39A7E",
                             "#B5C46A", "#D1A06A", "#6FB3A4", "#D08AA0", "#8E9CD0", "#D9B84E", "#A68FD0", "#6DBA87"), length(top)), top)
stn_w <- st_filter(lines_sf(stations), west)
o_w <- o_w |> mutate(change = case_when(to_new ~ "Switches to a new station",
                                       switched ~ "Switches to another existing station",
                                       TRUE ~ "Keeps its station"))
p_now <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = st_crop(subzone, west), fill = PAL$land, colour = PAL$land_line, linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_sf(data = o_w, aes(colour = ifelse(station_now %in% top, station_now, "other")), size = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(stn_w, existing), shape = 21, size = 1.8, colour = PAL$ink, fill = PAL$ground) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(pal_st, other = PAL$null), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Today: each block coloured by its main station") + mapt(12, crop = FALSE) +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA), plot.title = element_text(colour = PAL$ink, size = 12))
p_30 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = st_crop(subzone, west), fill = PAL$land, colour = PAL$land_line, linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_sf(data = o_w, aes(colour = change), size = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(stn_w, existing), shape = 21, size = 1.8, colour = PAL$ink, fill = PAL$ground) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(stn_w, !existing), aes(fill = kind), shape = 23, size = 2.4, colour = PAL$ink) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Switches to a new station" = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]],
                                 "Switches to another existing station" = PAL$loss,
                                 "Keeps its station" = PAL$null), name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Jurong Region Line" = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]], "Cross Island Line" = LINE_COLS[["CRL"]]), guide = "none") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2, override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
  labs(title = "With the JRL: blocks that change station") + mapt(12, crop = FALSE) +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA), plot.title = element_text(colour = PAL$ink, size = 12))
(p_now + p_30) & theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA))
```

::: {.subhead}
Same area and projection in both panels; circles are today's stations, diamonds the new
JRL stations. Across Singapore `r num(sum(scn$dom$switched))` of 10,817 blocks change their
main station, `r num(sum(scn$dom$to_new))` of them to a new one. Tengah's blocks, today at the
edge of several catchments, become the core of their own.
:::

## Distance matters about twice as much in the North-East and West as in the centre

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-va}
#| fig-height: 3.7
#| fig-width: 6.6
ggplot(lr, aes(lambda, reorder(region, lambda))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = th[["lambda"]], linetype = 2, colour = PAL$muted, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0, colour = PAL$accent, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(colour = PAL$accent, size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Distance exponent by region of the home block\n(more negative: distance matters more; dashed: one value for all)", y = NULL) +
  theme_ex03(12, grid = "x")
```
:::
::: {.note}
**Value-added.** Letting the effect of distance differ by region, a geographically
varying version of the model:

**North-East `r lrv("North-East")` and West `r lrv("West")`** against **Central `r lrv("Central")`.**
Newer towns are laid out around their own stop; central residents have several stations
to choose from. (The model shows the difference, not the reason.)

**It predicts hidden stations better:** R² `r round(m_of("R5", "R2_log"), 2)` against
`r round(m_of("M3", "R2_log"), 2)`; bias in the total `r round(m_of("R5", "bias_pct"))`% against
`r round(m_of("M3", "bias_pct"))`%.

**The conclusions hold:** new stations rank the same (`r round(r5$summ$rho_new, 2)`).
Only the western interchanges change: Jurong East loses
`r pct(-r5$cmp$change_pct_r5[r5$cmp$name == "Jurong East"])` instead of
`r pct(-r5$cmp$change_pct[r5$cmp$name == "Jurong East"])`.

[North and East estimates are too uncertain to read: too few stations there to tell
distance from attractiveness.]{.caveat}
:::
:::

## What the model supports, what it suggests, and what evidence is still missing

::: {.grid4}
::: {.q4}
[Residential demand]{.qh}

[Supports]{.k} A ranking of new stations by nearby HDB residents: Tengah Plantation,
Serangoon North, Pasir Ris East, Choa Chu Kang West on top.

[Suggests]{.k} These will be busy morning boarding points from opening.

[Needs]{.k} Private housing and new blocks; ridership at comparable new stations.
:::
::: {.q4}
[Jobs, campuses, airport]{.qh}

[Supports]{.k} Few HDB residents live near Aviation Park, Jurong Pier, Jurong Hill,
Loyang, Tukang and the Nanyang stations.

[Suggests]{.k} Nothing about their total use, or about opening dates.

[Needs]{.k} A model of morning arrivals with jobs and student numbers, and the
origin-destination data.
:::
::: {.q4}
[Existing stations]{.qh}

[Supports]{.k} Large shifts of HDB morning boardings away from Chinese Garden, Lakeside,
Pioneer, Bukit Batok and Kovan.

[Suggests]{.k} Lighter entry and access demand at those stations.

[Needs]{.k} Train routing and capacity before any claim about crowding; a bus-network
study before any feeder change.
:::
::: {.q4}
[Further validation]{.qh}

[Supports]{.k} The model ranks today's stations well (`r sprintf("%.2f", m_of("M3", "spearman"))`)
and its conclusions survive the sensitivity checks.

[Suggests]{.k} The regional model is the better guide in the West and North-East.

[Needs]{.k} A before-and-after test at a real opening; walking-network distances
instead of straight lines.
:::
:::

`r src` The brief's "public-safety" and "peace-keeping" implications are carry-overs from Take-home 2 and do not apply here.
